sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The holotype soldier is deposited in the Ahmad collection of the Zoology Department, University of the Punjab, Lahore; type locality Teknaf, Bangladesh. In the literature the species has been misidentified as G. chinpingensis Tsai & Chen. Distribution: Gailikhola, West Bengal, India, and elsewhere.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown with a smoky tinge; anteclypeus brownish yellow; labrum and antennae pale brown; pronotum dark brown; femora brown, tibiae and tarsi yellowish brown; wings pale smoky brown; abdomen dark brown. Head sparsely hairy; labral margin and body with several setae. Head circular, sides nearly parallel; length to the mandibular base 1.07—1.17 mm, width including the eyes 1.11—1.22 mm; Y-shaped suture not visible. Eyes slightly convex, lower margin almost straight; greatest diameter 0.28—0.31 mm, least diameter 0.23—0.25 mm. Ocelli small, oval, length 0.07—0.10 mm, width 0.06—0.09 mm, not touching the eyes (eye—ocellus distance 0.02—0.03 mm). Antennae 13—15-segmented; segments 2 and 3 subequal. Labrum wider than long, sides slightly convex, anterior margin almost straight. Mandibles of the typical tree-termite type. Pronotum almost rectangular, length 0.64—0.71 mm, width 1.10—1.32 mm; anterior margin deeply incurved, anterior lateral angles broadly rounded; sides convex; posterior margin slightly incurved. Tibial spur formula 3:3:3. Wings as in the genus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head red-brown, dark brown on the frons near the mandibular base; mandibles black, red-black behind; antennae and labrum brownish yellow; pronotum pale brown; legs pale brown, paler than the pronotum; abdomen pale brown. Head and body sparsely hairy. Body length 7.62—8.10 mm. Head capsule almost rectangular, distinctly longer than wide, length to the mandibular base 1.93—2.23 mm, about 1.6 times the width (1.3—1.4 mm); sides almost straight, posterior margin rounded; epicranial suture present; frons sloping forwards at about 45°, concave in the middle; a frontal projection at the base of the anterior margin of the slope; anterior lateral angles of the head rounded, not pointed. Antennae 12—14-segmented; segments 3 and 4 shortest. Anteclypeus thin, translucent, band-like; postclypeus indistinct from the frons, dark brown and hairy. Labrum almost rectangular, wider than long; length 0.18 mm, width 0.38 mm. Mandibles short, length 0.93—1.06 mm, thick, from less than half to about half the head length; left mandible with 3 marginal teeth, teeth 1 and 2 adjacent in the distal third, tooth 3 central and separated by a rounded incurved margin; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth, tooth 1 about at the midpoint, tooth 2 below it. Postmentum long, club-shaped, with a long narrow waist, the waist width less than half the greatest width; length 1.27—1.53 mm, greatest width 0.50—0.53 mm, waist width 0.20—0.26 mm. Pronotum flat, rectangular, narrower than the head; length 0.56—0.75 mm, width 1.19—1.44 mm; anterior margin rather deeply incurved; sides slightly convex; posterior margin almost straight, slightly incurved in the middle. Meso- and metanotum almost as wide as the pronotum. Legs short, thick, apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate, tergite 10 not sclerotized.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pseudoworker: head capsule and antennae pale brown; labrum slightly darker; pronotum slightly paler than the head; abdomen milky white. Head capsule almost circular, length to the mandibular base almost equal to the width (length 1.25 mm, width 1.25—1.28 mm). Eyes and ocelli indistinguishable. Antennae short, 12-segmented, the segments short and wide. Mandibles of the typical tree-termite type. Pronotum flat, slightly narrower than the head, anterior margin distinctly incurved. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.
